nodes.label: UMLFlow Project Configuration
nodes.rationale: Source code is the source of truth; diagrams under output.dir are treated as generated views. UMLFlow only writes the 'inferredScope' fields so human-authored diagram definitions and overrides are never clobbered by regeneration.

nodes.label: Analysis Scope Settings
nodes.rationale: Tests, specs, __tests__/test/tests directories and .d.ts declaration files are excluded so diagrams reflect production call structure rather than test scaffolding. maxFileSize (1MB) and maxCallDepth (6) bound analysis cost and keep sequence diagrams readable instead of exhaustively deep.

nodes.label: Inferred Scope
nodes.rationale: A natural-language query (e.g. 'login', 'orders') is resolved once into a concrete scope - files, components, entryPoints, entities - and cached with an inferredAt timestamp. This makes diagram regeneration deterministic and cheap: the expensive semantic resolution is not repeated on every update.

nodes.label: Pre-commit Check Hook
nodes.rationale: git.hooks.pre-commit is wired to 'check' rather than 'update' - commits fail when diagrams drift from code instead of silently rewriting generated files inside a commit, keeping the diff authored by the developer.

nodes.label: UMLFlow Semantic Facts Store
nodes.rationale: Facts carry a 'source' field: entries with source 'user' are human-declared and never overwritten, while 'semantic-inference' entries (e.g. established by Claude) are computed once and reused. This separation lets automated inference improve over time without ever discarding human intent. The file header is duplicated five times, suggesting the header is re-prepended on each write rather than rewritten - likely a bug.

nodes.label: Logger Ignore Rule
nodes.rationale: Logger is flagged ignore:true because a cross-cutting utility called from nearly every service would add noise to every sequence diagram without conveying domain meaning. It is still discovered by analysis (it appears in checkout-flow's inferredScope components) but suppressed at render time.

nodes.label: OrderController.create Use Case Naming
nodes.rationale: A user-declared useCase name ('Place order') overrides the name UMLFlow would otherwise derive from the operation identifier, which is why this use case renders without the '?' uncertainty marker that Login and Get Order carry.

nodes.label: Derived Use Case Name Marker
nodes.rationale: Use case names guessed from operation identifiers are suffixed with '?' and counted in the analysis notes, so a reader can tell machine-derived labels from human-declared ones and knows exactly which names to correct in semantics.yaml.

nodes.label: Login Flow Sequence Diagram
nodes.rationale: Generated content is fenced by UMLFLOW GENERATED BEGIN/END markers while MANUAL BEGIN/END blocks (both inside and outside the mermaid fence) survive regeneration, so hand-written notes can coexist with a fully regenerated diagram.

nodes.label: PaymentGateway
nodes.rationale: Payment is a two-step authorize-then-capture interaction against the gateway rather than a single charge call, which keeps the funds hold separable from settlement in the order flow.

nodes.label: Main Flows Sequence Diagram
nodes.rationale: Main Flows is an aggregate view: it re-renders every entry-point flow (login, place order, get order) in one diagram, so the same interactions also appear in the narrower login-flow and checkout-flow diagrams.

nodes.label: audit_log Entity
nodes.rationale: audit_log is named in raw table form (lowercase, BIGSERIAL id) unlike the class-named User/Order/OrderItem entities, indicating it is picked up from SQL/migration sources rather than from a TypeScript entity class.
